portfolio_level_findings.finding: Of 14 repositories, 6 define AWS infrastructure in CloudFormation/SAM, 1 (legacy-pricing-cgi) carries only Kubernetes manifests with no AWS IaC, and 7 have no IaC of any kind. Where IaC exists it is consistently CloudFormation/SAM — the fragmentation is coverage, not tool choice.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: INF-Q10 evidence across all repos: infra/template.yaml (modern-catalog-graphql, modern-payments-api), two CloudFormation templates (modern-claims-agent), infra/ecs.yaml (modern-orders-service), App Runner template (monolith), infrastructure/shipping-alb.yaml (legacy-shipping-api, edge only), k8s/deployment.yaml (legacy-pricing-cgi); no IaC files found in the nine remaining legacy repos.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Adopt CloudFormation/SAM as the single portfolio IaC standard (it is already the de-facto choice) and treat IaC coverage — not tool selection — as the Phase 0 goal. Publish a reusable template library seeded from modern-payments-api and monolith.
portfolio_level_findings.contextual_annotations: Provides context for the INF-Q10 Foundational Blocker: the portfolio has a usable IaC standard, so remediation is template authoring rather than tool evaluation — verify that the existing templates are parameterised enough to reuse.

portfolio_level_findings.finding: No centralized observability stack spans the portfolio. Distributed tracing (OPS-Q1) scores below 3 in 12 of 14 repos, SLOs (OPS-Q2), metrics (OPS-Q3) and alerting (OPS-Q4) score 1 in 13 of 14, and no shared log group, dashboard or metric namespace convention is referenced by any repo. Each service observes itself, or not at all.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: OPS-Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 findings in all 14 per-repo reports; only modern-payments-api (Lambda Powertools) and modern-claims-agent show any structured instrumentation.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Stand up one observability platform in Phase 0 — CloudWatch (logs, metrics, alarms) plus ADOT/X-Ray for traces — with a mandated metric namespace and log-group naming convention, and propagate trace context at every service edge.
portfolio_level_findings.contextual_annotations: Provides context for the OPS-Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 Foundational Blockers: these are a single platform gap repeated 14 times, not 14 independent service gaps — verify whether an unassessed central monitoring account already exists before funding per-service work.

portfolio_level_findings.finding: No service-to-service dependencies were declared in the portfolio configuration and none could be inferred from the per-repo report text — no report names another assessed repository as a runtime dependency. With no edges, no cycles exist.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: No `dependency_overrides` supplied; a scan of all 14 per-repo report texts for the other 13 repo names produced only incidental matches in generic recommendation prose, not evidence of inter-service calls.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Supply `dependency_overrides` (or run a runtime dependency discovery) before committing to the roadmap sequencing. The score reflects an absence of evidence, not a verified absence of coupling.
portfolio_level_findings.contextual_annotations: Low confidence. This score should be re-derived once dependency data is available — verify by inspecting service clients, API gateways and shared databases outside the assessed repositories.

portfolio_level_findings.finding: 14 distinct language/runtime stacks across 14 repositories (diversity score 1.0 — one stack per service): VB6, CFML, Python 2.7, Java 5, Java 6, COBOL/JCL, C++, Node.js/Express 3, Ruby 1.8.7, TypeScript (x2), Python (x2) and PHP 8.2. Six databases span four engines across commercial and open-source licensing. No language maps consistently to a service archetype — ten of fourteen repos share the `stateful-crud` archetype yet use ten different stacks, so this is accidental sprawl rather than intentional polyglot.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: metadata.language and metadata.service_archetype across all 14 reports; INF-Q2 evidence for the database engines.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Declare two or three supported runtimes (the portfolio already clusters on TypeScript/Node 20 and Python 3.12) and route every modernization target onto them; treat the EOL stacks (VB6, CFML, Python 2.7, Java 5/6, Ruby 1.8.7) as retirement candidates rather than upgrade candidates.
portfolio_level_findings.contextual_annotations: Provides context for the APP-Q1 Foundational Blocker: the runtime-currency gap is portfolio-wide fragmentation, so per-repo upgrades will not converge without a declared target runtime set.

portfolio_level_findings.finding: Each repository manages security independently. Pipeline security scanning (SEC-Q7) scores below 3 in all 14 repos, dependency/patch management (SEC-Q6) below 3 in 12, and no shared WAF WebACL, centralized scanning service or common Secrets Manager/IAM convention appears in any report.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: SEC-Q2 through SEC-Q7 findings across all 14 reports; only modern-payments-api, modern-catalog-graphql and monolith show managed secret handling.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Establish one security baseline in Phase 0: centralized SAST/SCA/IaC scanning in a shared pipeline template, a single WAF WebACL in front of all internet-facing entry points, Secrets Manager for every credential, and organization-wide threat detection and posture management.
portfolio_level_findings.contextual_annotations: Provides context for the SEC-Q4/Q5/Q6/Q7 Foundational Blockers: a single shared pipeline and WAF would close part of these gaps across all repos at once — verify which accounts already have GuardDuty/Security Hub enabled.
